rows.why: Check the news first — we expect 34.8 but the line is 19.5. A gap this big usually means the sportsbook knows something (a role change, an injury). We expect about 34.8 rushing yards vs the 19.5 line. We give the over 82% (needs 56% per pick on Underdog); recent games and the matchup both point higher
rows.why_long: Underdog higher 19.5 needs 56% per pick for your entry; fair view 85% (fanduel 46.5, moved to this line). Averaging 36.9 over the last 8 games, higher than 19.5 in 42% of them (raw 73%, shrunk 83%). LA is league-average vs RBs → projects 34.8 (raw 63%, shrunk 82%).
why_points: The pick: Rush yds higher 19.5 on Underdog. Each pick has to win 56% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the sportsbooks' fair view (fanduel 46.5, moved to this line) is 85%.
Other apps: PrizePicks 46.5. This is the best number for the higher side.
Game log, most recent first: 7, 42, -1, 10, 61, 16, 23, 79. Weighted average 36.9; went higher than 19.5 in 4 of 8 games (42% recency-weighted).
Trending down: last 3 games average 16.0 vs 37.8 in the games before.
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±24.1, so the line is 0.7 of those swings below his average (standard deviations) — a meaningful gap.
Teammate out: +3.5 car with Jeremiyah Love OUT. When a lead player sits, his teammates pick up about half his work (NFL 2019-25), so this prop is scaled +49%.
Matchup: LA is about league-average against RBs.
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): -2% on his average.
PFF: LA plays man on 31% of coverage snaps (his opponents so far 26%); he gains 0.96 yds/route vs man and 0.83 vs zone → +1% from scheme.
PFF: LA allows 1.36 yds/route to RBs after adjusting for the offenses it faced (league 1.18) → +15% against his usual opponents.
PFF: 43% of his targets are short (0-9 yds) (league 48%); LA allows 6.3 yds/target there (league 6.4) → +3% from depth.
PFF: He lines up in the slot 96% of the time; LA's slot defenders allow 1.49 yds per coverage snap (league 1.58, tighter).
PFF: ARI's run blocking vs LA's run defense: 1.1 yds before contact per carry expected (his usual 1.2, league 1.2); he adds 3.0 after contact → -2% per carry.
Projection: we expect 34.8 rushing yards on average; in a typical game 24.4 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 4.9 above the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 73% and the matchup 63%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 83%, matchup 82%.
Bottom line: we give it 82% to win and it needs 56%. The edge is the difference: +25.7 points; that works out to about +46¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
